questions.text: आयरन की सर्वाधिक स्थायी ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था है :
questions.text_english: The most stable oxidation state of Iron is :
questions.solution: The most stable oxidation state of Iron (Fe) is +3. Iron has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d6 4s2. The +3 oxidation state (Fe3+) gives a half-filled 3d5 configuration, which is particularly stable due to extra stability associated with half-filled orbitals. Option A (+2) is less stable, option C (+4) is uncommon for iron, and option D (–2) is not observed for iron under normal conditions.
questions.solution_hindi: आयरन (Fe) की सर्वाधिक स्थायी ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था +3 है। Fe का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास [Ar] 3d6 4s2 है। +3 अवस्था (Fe3+) में अर्धपूर्ण 3d5 विन्यास प्राप्त होता है जो विशेष स्थायित्व प्रदान करता है।

questions.text: CH3MgBr और CO2 में अभिक्रिया के पश्चात जल-अपघटन करने पर निर्मित उत्पाद है :
questions.text_english: The product formed as a result of reaction of CH3MgBr and CO2 followed by hydrolysis is :
questions.solution: When CH3MgBr (a Grignard reagent) reacts with CO2, it forms a magnesium salt intermediate (CH3COOMgBr). Upon hydrolysis with water, this intermediate gives acetic acid (CH3COOH). The methyl group of CH3MgBr acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbon of CO2, extending the carbon chain by one carbon and yielding a carboxylic acid. Hence option D is correct. Options A and B would require reaction with an aldehyde or ketone respectively, and option C (formic acid) would require HMgBr reacting with CO2.
questions.solution_hindi: CH3MgBr (ग्रीन्यार अभिकर्मक) CO2 के साथ अभिक्रिया करके मैग्नीशियम लवण मध्यवर्ती (CH3COOMgBr) बनाता है। जल-अपघटन पर एसिटिक अम्ल (CH3COOH) प्राप्त होता है।

questions.text: न्यूक्लियोटाइड संघटित होते हैं एक :
questions.text_english: Nucleotides are composed of a :

options.A: पेन्टोस शर्करा और फ़ॉस्फ़ोरिक अम्ल से
options.B: नाइट्रोजन युक्त क्षारक, पेन्टोस शर्करा और फ़ॉस्फ़ोरिक अम्ल से
options.C: नाइट्रोजन युक्त क्षारक और फ़ॉस्फ़ोरिक अम्ल से
options.D: पेन्टोस शर्करा और नाइट्रोजन युक्त क्षारक से

options_english.B: nitrogenous base, pentose sugar and phosphoric acid

questions.solution: A nucleotide is composed of three components: a nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine), a pentose sugar (ribose in RNA or deoxyribose in DNA), and a phosphoric acid group. A nucleoside consists of only the nitrogenous base and pentose sugar. When phosphoric acid is added to a nucleoside, it becomes a nucleotide. Options A, C, and D are incomplete as each omits one of the three essential components of a nucleotide.
questions.solution_hindi: एक न्यूक्लियोटाइड तीन घटकों से मिलकर बना होता है: नाइट्रोजन युक्त क्षारक, पेन्टोस शर्करा और फ़ॉस्फ़ोरिक अम्ल। अन्य विकल्प अपूर्ण हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित ऐल्किल हैलाइडों में से कौन-सा SN1 अभिक्रिया सर्वाधिक शीघ्रता से करता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following alkyl halides will undergo SN1 reaction most readily ?
questions.solution: In SN1 reactions, the rate-determining step is the formation of a carbocation, which depends on the ease of C–X bond cleavage. All four options are tertiary halides forming the same tertiary carbocation, so the leaving group ability determines the rate. The leaving group ability follows the order: I– > Br– > Cl– > F–. Since iodide (I–) is the best leaving group due to its large size and high polarizability, (CH3)3C–I undergoes SN1 most readily. Hence option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: SN1 अभिक्रिया में C–X बंध के टूटने की सुगमता दर निर्धारित करती है। I– सबसे अच्छा विदायी समूह है क्योंकि यह सबसे बड़ा और सबसे अधिक ध्रुवणीय है। अत: (CH3)3C–I सबसे शीघ्र SN1 अभिक्रिया करता है।

questions.text: फ़ीनॉल, बेन्ज़ीन में द्वितय बनाता है जिसका वान्ट हॉफ कारक 0·54 है । इसकी संगुणन मात्रा है :
questions.text_english: Phenol dimerises in benzene having van't Hoff factor 0·54. Its degree of association is :
questions.solution: For association (dimerisation, n=2), the van't Hoff factor i = 1 – α/2, where α is the degree of association. Given i = 0.54: 0.54 = 1 – α/2, so α/2 = 1 – 0.54 = 0.46, therefore α = 0.92. The degree of association is 0.92. Option C is correct. Options A and B confuse the van't Hoff factor with the degree of association, and option D is incorrect arithmetically.

questions.text:
कोई अभिक्रिया A2 + B2 → 2AB निम्न क्रियाविधि द्वारा होती है :
A2 → A + A (मंद)
A + B2 → AB + B (तेज)
A + B → AB (तेज)
इसकी कोटि होगी :
questions.text_english:
A reaction A2 + B2 → 2AB occurs by the following mechanism :
A2 → A + A (slow)
A + B2 → AB + B (fast)
A + B → AB (fast)
Its order would be :
questions.solution: The order of a reaction is determined by the slowest (rate-determining) step. The slow step here is A2 → A + A, which involves only one molecule of A2. Therefore, the rate of reaction depends only on the concentration of A2 raised to the first power: Rate = k[A2]. The overall order of reaction is 1 (first order). Options B, C, and D are incorrect because the rate does not depend on B2 at all (as the steps involving B2 are fast), and the slow step involves only A2 to the first power.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिक्रिया की कोटि मंद (दर-निर्धारक) पद द्वारा निर्धारित होती है। मंद पद A2 → A + A है जिसमें केवल A2 सम्मिलित है। अत: दर = k[A2], कोटि = 1।

questions.text: सोडा लाइम के साथ सोडियम बेन्ज़ोएट को गर्म करने पर विकार्बोक्सिलन से बनता है :
questions.text_english: Decarboxylation of sodium benzoate on heating with soda lime gives :
questions.solution: When sodium benzoate (C6H5COONa) is heated with soda lime (NaOH + CaO), decarboxylation occurs. The –COO– group is removed as CO2, and the remaining C6H5– group picks up hydrogen to form benzene (C6H6). This reaction is used to prepare arenes from their sodium salts of carboxylic acids. Option D (toluene) would be formed if sodium phenyl acetate were used instead. Options B and C are incorrect products for this reaction.
questions.solution_hindi: सोडियम बेन्ज़ोएट को सोडा लाइम के साथ गर्म करने पर विकार्बोक्सिलन होता है और –COO– समूह CO2 के रूप में निकल जाता है, जिससे बेन्ज़ीन बनती है।

questions.text: CH3–C(=O)–CH2–C(=O)–H का आई.यू.पी.ए.सी. (IUPAC) नाम है :
questions.text_english: The IUPAC name of CH3–C(=O)–CH2–C(=O)–H is :
questions.solution: The compound CH3–CO–CH2–CHO is a 4-carbon chain. The principal functional group is the aldehyde (–CHO), which gets the lowest locant (C-1). Numbering from the aldehyde end: C1 = CHO, C2 = CH2, C3 = CO (ketone), C4 = CH3. The parent chain is butanal (4 carbons ending in –al). The keto group at C3 is indicated as 3-oxo. Therefore, the IUPAC name is 3-oxobutanal. Option C is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: यौगिक CH3–CO–CH2–CHO में एल्डिहाइड समूह को C-1 पर रखने पर, C-3 पर कीटो समूह है। अत: IUPAC नाम 3-ऑक्सोब्यूटेनैल है।

questions.text: 573 K पर Cu के साथ तृतीयक ऐल्कोहॉलों के निर्जलन से बनता है :
questions.text_english: Dehydration of tertiary alcohols with Cu at 573 K gives :
questions.solution: When tertiary alcohols are passed over heated copper at 573 K (dehydration conditions), they undergo elimination of water to form alkenes. This is a dehydration reaction. Primary alcohols at 573 K with Cu undergo dehydrogenation to give aldehydes, and secondary alcohols give ketones. However, tertiary alcohols lack an alpha hydrogen suitable for dehydrogenation and instead undergo dehydration to form alkenes. Hence option B is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: 573 K पर Cu के साथ तृतीयक ऐल्कोहॉल निर्जलन अभिक्रिया द्वारा ऐल्कीन बनाते हैं। प्राथमिक ऐल्कोहॉल इसी ताप पर ऐल्डिहाइड देते हैं और द्वितीयक ऐल्कोहॉल कीटोन देते हैं।

questions.text: आरेनिअस समीकरण में जब 1/T के साथ log k का ग्राफ खींचा जाता है, तो एक सीधी रेखा प्राप्त होती है जिसकी :
questions.text_english: In the Arrhenius equation, when log k is plotted against 1/T, a straight line is obtained whose :

options.A: ढाल A/R है और अंत:खंड Ea है।
options.B: ढाल A है और अंत:खंड –Ea/R है।
options.C: ढाल –Ea/RT है और अंत:खंड log A है।
options.D: ढाल –Ea/(2.303R) है और अंत:खंड log A है।

options_english.A: slope is A/R and intercept is Ea.
options_english.B: slope is A and intercept is –Ea/R.
options_english.C: slope is –Ea/RT and intercept is log A.
options_english.D: slope is –Ea/(2.303R) and intercept is log A.

questions.solution: The Arrhenius equation is k = A·e^(–Ea/RT). Taking log on both sides: log k = log A – Ea/(2.303RT). Comparing with y = mx + c: when log k is plotted against 1/T, slope = –Ea/(2.303R) and y-intercept = log A. Option D is correct. Option C is wrong because the slope contains RT in the denominator which would make it variable (dependent on T), not a constant slope.
questions.solution_hindi: आरेनिअस समीकरण से: log k = log A – Ea/(2.303RT)। यह y = mx + c के रूप में है जहाँ ढाल = –Ea/(2.303R) और अंत:खंड = log A।

questions.text: कक्ष ताप पर फ़ीनॉल, जलीय ब्रोमीन के साथ अभिक्रिया करके देता है :
questions.text_english: Phenol on reaction with aqueous bromine at room temperature gives :
questions.solution: Phenol is highly activated towards electrophilic aromatic substitution due to the strong +M effect of the –OH group, which donates electron density to the ortho and para positions. When phenol reacts with aqueous bromine water (Br2/H2O) at room temperature, all three activated positions (ortho-2, ortho-6, and para-4) are simultaneously brominated, giving 2,4,6-tribromophenol as a white precipitate. This reaction is so fast that no catalyst is needed, unlike benzene bromination. Hence option D is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: फ़ीनॉल में –OH समूह +M प्रभाव द्वारा ऑर्थो और पैरा स्थानों पर इलेक्ट्रॉन घनत्व बढ़ाता है। जलीय ब्रोमीन से कक्ष ताप पर तीनों सक्रिय स्थानों (2, 4, 6) पर एक साथ ब्रोमीनन होकर 2,4,6-ट्राइब्रोमोफ़ीनॉल बनता है।

questions.text: प्रोटीन में ऐमीनो अम्लों का विशिष्ट क्रम में व्यवस्थित होना कहलाता है :
questions.text_english: The specific sequence in which amino acids are arranged in a protein is called :
questions.solution: The primary structure of a protein refers to the specific sequence in which amino acids are covalently linked to each other through peptide bonds. The secondary structure refers to the coiling or folding of the polypeptide chain (e.g., alpha-helix, beta-sheet). The tertiary structure is the three-dimensional folding of the protein, and quaternary structure involves the arrangement of multiple polypeptide subunits. Hence option B is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रोटीन की प्राथमिक संरचना ऐमीनो अम्लों के पेप्टाइड बंधों द्वारा जुड़ने के विशिष्ट अनुक्रम को दर्शाती है। द्वितीयक संरचना कुंडलन/वलन, तृतीयक संरचना त्रि-आयामी विन्यास और चतुष्क संरचना उपइकाइयों की व्यवस्था है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : अमोनिया की तुलना में ऐनिलीन प्रबलतर क्षारक है ।
कारण (R) : ऐनिलीन में नाइट्रोजन परमाणु पर उपस्थित असहभाजित इलेक्ट्रॉन युगल, अनुनाद के कारण प्रोटॉनन के लिए कम उपलब्ध होता है ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Aniline is a stronger base than ammonia.
Reason (R) : The unshared electron pair on nitrogen atom in aniline becomes less available for protonation due to resonance.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथन दिए गए हैं — एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है। सही उत्तर (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से चुनकर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given — one labelled Assertion (A) and the other Reason (R). Select the correct answer from (A), (B), (C) and (D).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is false: Aniline is actually a weaker base than ammonia, not stronger. In aniline, the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalized into the benzene ring through resonance, making it less available for protonation. Ammonia has no such resonance delocalization, so its lone pair is freely available, making it a stronger base than aniline (pKb of NH3 ≈ 4.74, pKb of aniline ≈ 9.38). However, Reason (R) is true: the lone pair in aniline does become less available due to resonance. Hence option D is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन (A) गलत है: ऐनिलीन अमोनिया की तुलना में दुर्बल क्षारक है। ऐनिलीन में N पर असहभाजित इलेक्ट्रॉन युगल अनुनाद के कारण बेंज़ीन वलय में विस्थानित हो जाता है। कारण (R) सही है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : CH3–COOH की तुलना में O2N–CH2–COOH का pKa मान निम्नतर होता है ।
कारण (R) : –NO2 समूह इलेक्ट्रॉन अपनयन प्रभाव दर्शाता है जो O2N–CH2–COOH का अम्लीय अभिलक्षण बढ़ा देता है ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : The pKa of O2N–CH2–COOH is lower than that of CH3–COOH.
Reason (R) : –NO2 group shows electron withdrawing effect which increases the acidic character of O2N–CH2–COOH.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथन दिए गए हैं — एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given — one labelled Assertion (A) and the other Reason (R).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both statements are true and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). A lower pKa means a stronger acid. The –NO2 group is strongly electron-withdrawing (by both inductive and resonance effects). In O2N–CH2–COOH, the –NO2 group withdraws electron density from the –COOH group through the –CH2– chain, stabilizing the carboxylate anion (O2N–CH2–COO–) formed after proton loss. This increased stability of the conjugate base makes the acid stronger (lower pKa) compared to CH3–COOH, where –CH3 is electron-donating. Hence option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: दोनों कथन सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है। –NO2 समूह इलेक्ट्रॉन अपनयन प्रभाव द्वारा कार्बोक्सिलेट आयन को स्थायित्व देता है जिससे अम्ल प्रबल होता है (pKa निम्न)।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : संक्रमण धातुओं की कणन एन्थैल्पी उच्च होती है ।
कारण (R) : ऐसा इसलिए है क्योंकि संक्रमण धातुओं के गलनांक निम्न होते हैं ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Transition metals have high enthalpy of atomization.
Reason (R) : This is because transition metals have low melting points.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथन दिए गए हैं — एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given — one labelled Assertion (A) and the other Reason (R).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true: Transition metals do have high enthalpy of atomization because of the large number of unpaired d-electrons available for metallic bonding, resulting in very strong interatomic interactions. Reason (R) is false: Transition metals actually have very HIGH melting and boiling points (e.g., W melts at 3422°C), not low. The high enthalpy of atomization and the high melting points are related — both are due to strong metallic bonding. The Reason falsely states that they have low melting points. Hence option C is correct.

questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : When NaCl is added in water, elevation in boiling point is observed.
Reason (R) : Elevation in boiling point is a colligative property.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथन दिए गए हैं — एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given — one labelled Assertion (A) and the other Reason (R).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). When NaCl is dissolved in water, it increases the number of solute particles (Na+ and Cl– ions), which raises the boiling point of the solution. Elevation in boiling point (ΔTb = Kb × m × i) is indeed a colligative property, meaning it depends only on the number of solute particles and not on their nature. The Reason thus correctly explains the Assertion. Hence option A is correct.

questions.text_english:
(a) Draw the structures of major monohalo products in each of the following reactions :
(i) Vinylbenzene (styrene) + HBr →
(ii) Cyclohexane + Br2 (UV light) →

OR

(b) Give reasons for the following :
(i) Grignard reagent should be prepared under anhydrous conditions.
(ii) Alkyl halides give alcohol with aqueous KOH whereas in the presence of alcoholic KOH, alkenes are formed.

key_points: (a)(i) Product: 1-bromo-1-phenylethane (Markovnikov addition of HBr to styrene, Br attaches to the more substituted carbon bearing the phenyl group)
(a)(ii) Product: bromocyclohexane (free radical substitution under UV light replaces one H with Br)
(b)(i) Grignard reagents react with water to form hydrocarbons; anhydrous conditions prevent decomposition
(b)(ii) Aqueous KOH provides OH– for nucleophilic substitution (SN2) giving alcohol; alcoholic KOH provides bulky alkoxide that acts as a base causing E2 elimination giving alkene

questions.solution:
Answer (a): For reaction (i), styrene (C6H5–CH=CH2) reacts with HBr following Markovnikov's rule. The proton adds to the terminal carbon (CH2) and Br adds to the benzylic carbon, giving 1-bromo-1-phenylethane (C6H5–CHBr–CH3) as the major product because the benzylic carbocation intermediate is more stable. For reaction (ii), cyclohexane reacts with Br2 under UV light via free radical substitution. Since all H atoms in cyclohexane are equivalent, the only product is bromocyclohexane (C6H11Br).

Answer (b)(i): Grignard reagents (RMgX) are extremely reactive towards protic sources. Water reacts immediately with the C–Mg bond: RMgX + H2O → RH + Mg(OH)X. This destroys the reagent before it can be used. Therefore, anhydrous (moisture-free) conditions are essential during preparation and use.

Answer (b)(ii): Aqueous KOH is a dilute, polar medium providing free OH– ions. In polar protic solvents, OH– acts as a nucleophile and attacks the carbon bearing the halogen via SN2 mechanism, displacing the halide and forming an alcohol. Alcoholic KOH (in ethanol) provides a less solvated, more basic environment. The bulky ethoxide/hydroxide acts primarily as a base, abstracting a beta hydrogen and promoting E2 elimination to form an alkene.

What happens when D-glucose is treated with the following reagents ?
(a) Br2 water
(b) HCN

key_points: (a) Br2 water oxidizes the aldehyde group (–CHO) of D-glucose to a carboxyl group (–COOH), forming D-gluconic acid
(b) HCN adds to the aldehyde group of D-glucose in a nucleophilic addition reaction, forming glucose cyanohydrin (an alpha-hydroxy nitrile with one additional carbon)

questions.solution: When D-glucose is treated with Br2 water, the aldehyde group (–CHO) present at C-1 is selectively oxidized to a carboxyl group (–COOH), forming D-gluconic acid. Br2 water is a mild oxidizing agent that oxidizes only the aldehyde group without affecting the other hydroxyl groups. When D-glucose is treated with HCN, the cyanide ion (CN–) acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of the aldehyde group in a nucleophilic addition reaction. This results in the formation of a cyanohydrin (glucose cyanohydrin), which has one extra carbon atom compared to glucose. This reaction is significant in the Kiliani synthesis for lengthening the carbon chain of sugars.

questions.text_english:
Write the chemical equations when :
(a) Pentan-3-one is treated with H2N–NH2 followed by heating with KOH in high boiling solvent such as ethylene glycol.
(b) Two molecules of (CH3)3C–CHO are treated with conc. NaOH.

key_points: (a) Wolff-Kishner reduction: pentan-3-one reacts with H2N-NH2 to form a hydrazone, then KOH/ethylene glycol at high temperature reduces it to pentane (CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3)
(b) Cannizzaro reaction: (CH3)3C-CHO has no alpha-hydrogen, so with conc. NaOH it undergoes disproportionation giving (CH3)3C-COONa (sodium pivalate) and (CH3)3C-CH2OH (neopentyl alcohol)

questions.solution:
For reaction (a): Pentan-3-one (CH3CH2COCH2CH3) first reacts with hydrazine (H2N–NH2) to form pentan-3-one hydrazone (CH3CH2C(=NNH2)CH2CH3). When this hydrazone is heated with KOH in a high-boiling solvent like ethylene glycol, the Wolff-Kishner reduction occurs and the C=O group is completely reduced to –CH2–, giving pentane (CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3) and N2 gas.

For reaction (b): (CH3)3C–CHO (trimethylacetaldehyde/pivalaldehyde) has no alpha-hydrogen (the carbon adjacent to C=O bears no H atoms because it is a quaternary carbon bearing three methyl groups). Therefore, it cannot undergo aldol condensation. Instead, it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated NaOH: one molecule is oxidized to (CH3)3C–COONa (sodium pivalate/trimethylacetate) and the other is reduced to (CH3)3C–CH2OH (neopentyl alcohol / 2,2-dimethyl-1-propanol). This is a disproportionation reaction where one molecule acts as an oxidizing agent and the other as a reducing agent.

आयरन इलेक्ट्रोड का विभव परिकलित कीजिए जिसमें Fe2+ आयन की सांद्रता 0·01 M है ।
(298 K पर E°Fe2+/Fe = –0·45 V)
[दिया गया है : log 10 = 1]
questions.text_english:
Calculate the potential of Iron electrode in which the concentration of Fe2+ ion is 0·01 M.
(E°Fe2+/Fe = –0·45 V at 298 K)
[Given : log 10 = 1]

key_points: Using Nernst equation: E = E° – (0.0591/n) × log(1/[Fe2+])
n = 2 for Fe2+/Fe electrode

questions.solution: The electrode reaction is Fe2+ + 2e– → Fe, where n = 2. Applying the Nernst equation at 298 K: E = E° – (0.0591/n) × log(1/[Fe2+]). Substituting the values: E = –0.45 – (0.0591/2) × log(1/0.01). Since 1/0.01 = 100 = 10², log(100) = 2. Therefore E = –0.45 – (0.02955 × 2) = –0.45 – 0.0591 = –0.5091 V. The potential of the iron electrode is –0.5091 V.

questions.text_english: Write two differences between order of reaction and molecularity of reaction.

key_points: Order is determined experimentally from rate law and can be zero, fractional, or integer; molecularity is a theoretical concept based on the number of reacting species in the elementary step and is always a positive integer
Order can be zero or fractional and applies to overall reaction; molecularity is always a whole number (1, 2, or 3) and applies only to elementary reactions

questions.solution: The order of a reaction is determined experimentally from the rate law expression and represents the sum of the powers of concentration terms in the rate equation. It can be zero, fractional, or a whole number. In contrast, molecularity is a theoretical concept defined as the total number of reactant molecules (or atoms or ions) participating in an elementary reaction step. Molecularity is always a positive whole number (1, 2, or 3) and can never be zero or fractional. Additionally, order applies to the overall reaction and may change with experimental conditions, while molecularity applies only to each individual elementary step of the mechanism.

questions.text: यौगिक (A) (C6H12O2), LiAlH4 से अपचयित होकर दो यौगिक (B) और (C) देता है । यौगिक (B) PCC के साथ ऑक्सीकृत होकर यौगिक (D) देता है जो तनु NaOH के साथ अभिकृत करके तदुपरान्त गर्म करने पर यौगिक (E) देता है । यौगिक (E) उत्प्रेरकीय हाइड्रोजनन करने पर यौगिक (C) देता है । यौगिक (D) और ऑक्सीकृत होकर यौगिक (F) देता है जो कि एकक्षारकीय अम्ल (अणु भार = 60) पाया गया । यौगिकों (A), (B), (C), (D), (E) और (F) की पहचान कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Compound (A) (C6H12O2) on reduction with LiAlH4 gives two compounds (B) and (C). The compound (B) on oxidation with PCC gives compound (D) which upon treatment with dilute NaOH and subsequent heating gives compound (E). Compound (E) on catalytic hydrogenation gives compound (C). The compound (D) is oxidized further to give compound (F) which is found to be a monobasic acid (Molecular weight = 60). Identify the compounds (A), (B), (C), (D), (E) and (F).

key_points: F is a monobasic acid with MW = 60: acetic acid (CH3COOH, MW = 60)
D is oxidized to F (acetic acid), so D is acetaldehyde (CH3CHO)
B is oxidized by PCC to D (CH3CHO), so B is ethanol (CH3CH2OH)
D (CH3CHO) undergoes aldol condensation with dil. NaOH then heating to give E: crotonaldehyde (CH3CH=CHCHO) via aldol condensation of two molecules of acetaldehyde

E on catalytic hydrogenation gives C; C must be n-butanol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH) ... actually E (crotonaldehyde) on hydrogenation gives butyraldehyde or n-butanol; since E gives C which is also given by LiAlH4 reduction of A, C = n-butanol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH)

A (C6H12O2) on reduction gives B (CH3CH2OH) and C (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH); A is an ester: ethyl butyrate (CH3CH2CH2COOC2H5) or butyl acetate — since D is CH3CHO, B is ethanol; A gives ethanol and n-butanol; A is ethyl butanoate (C2H5COOC2H5) — but that gives two ethanol molecules; actually A is n-butyl acetate (CH3COO-C4H9) giving acetic acid path... Working backwards: B→D (PCC)→D=CH3CHO means B=CH3CH2OH (ethanol). C=product of E hydrogenation. E is aldol product of D: 2CH3CHO → CH3CH(OH)CH2CHO (aldol) → heat → CH3CH=CHCHO (crotonaldehyde). Hydrogenation of crotonaldehyde → butanal or n-butanol. Since C is also from LiAlH4 reduction of A, C = n-butanol. A (C6H12O2) gives ethanol (B) and n-butanol (C) on LiAlH4 reduction — A is an ester: n-butyl acetate (CH3COOC4H9, MW=116, C6H12O2 ✓)

questions.solution: Working backwards from the given clues: Compound F is a monobasic acid with molecular weight 60, which corresponds to acetic acid (CH3COOH). Since D is oxidized to give F (acetic acid), compound D must be acetaldehyde (CH3CHO). Since B is oxidized by PCC (a mild oxidant for primary alcohols to aldehydes) to give D (CH3CHO), compound B is ethanol (CH3CH2OH). Compound D (acetaldehyde) undergoes aldol condensation with dilute NaOH to give 3-hydroxybutanal, which on subsequent heating undergoes dehydration to give E = crotonaldehyde (CH3CH=CH–CHO, but-2-enal). Compound E on catalytic hydrogenation gives C = n-butanol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH). Now, compound A (C6H12O2) on reduction with LiAlH4 gives B (ethanol) and C (n-butanol). This means A is an ester whose acid part gives ethanol and alcohol part gives n-butanol on reduction. Therefore, A is n-butyl acetate (CH3COO–CH2CH2CH2CH3), molecular formula C6H12O2 (MW = 116), which is confirmed. Summary: A = n-butyl acetate, B = ethanol, C = n-butanol, D = acetaldehyde, E = crotonaldehyde (but-2-enal), F = acetic acid.

questions.text_english:
Answer the following : (any three)
(a) What is peptide linkage ?
(b) What type of bonds hold a DNA double helix together ?
(c) Which one of the following is a polysaccharide ? Sucrose, Glucose, Starch, Fructose
(d) Give one example each for water-soluble vitamins and fat-soluble vitamins.

key_points: (a) Peptide linkage is the amide bond (–CO–NH–) formed between the –COOH group of one amino acid and the –NH2 group of another with the elimination of water
(b) Hydrogen bonds (between complementary base pairs: A–T and G–C) hold the two strands of DNA double helix together
(c) Starch is a polysaccharide; sucrose is a disaccharide; glucose and fructose are monosaccharides
(d) Water-soluble vitamin example: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) or Vitamin B; Fat-soluble vitamin example: Vitamin A, D, E, or K

questions.solution:
Answer (a): A peptide linkage (peptide bond) is the amide linkage formed when the carboxyl group (–COOH) of one amino acid reacts with the amino group (–NH2) of another amino acid with the elimination of a water molecule. It is represented as –CO–NH– and is the bond that links amino acids in a polypeptide chain.

Answer (b): The two complementary strands of the DNA double helix are held together by hydrogen bonds between the complementary nitrogenous bases. Adenine (A) pairs with Thymine (T) through two hydrogen bonds, and Guanine (G) pairs with Cytosine (C) through three hydrogen bonds.

Answer (c): Starch is a polysaccharide, as it is a polymer of glucose units. Sucrose is a disaccharide (glucose + fructose), while glucose and fructose are monosaccharides.

Answer (d): Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) and Vitamin B-complex (e.g., Vitamin B1 – thiamine) are water-soluble vitamins. Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble vitamins; for example, Vitamin A (retinol) is fat-soluble.

questions.text_english:
(a) Write the mechanism of the following reaction :
CH3CH2OH → (H+, 443 K) → CH2=CH2

(b) Write the main product in each of the following reactions :
(i) CH3–CH2–CH=CH2 → (a) B2H6 / (b) 3H2O2/OH–
(ii) Cyclohexanol → (a) aq. NaOH / (b) CO2, H+

key_points: (a) Mechanism: Step 1 - protonation of OH to form oxonium ion; Step 2 - loss of water to form carbocation (CH3CH2+); Step 3 - loss of a proton from beta carbon to give ethylene
(b)(i) Hydroboration-oxidation is anti-Markovnikov addition; but-1-ene gives 1-butanol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH)

(b)(ii) Cyclohexanol reacts with aq. NaOH then CO2, H+ via Kolbe-Schmitt type or Reimer-Tiemann... actually cyclohexanol is an alcohol not phenol. With aq. NaOH it forms sodium cyclohexoxide; with CO2 and H+ it gives cyclohexanol back. Actually this reaction is for phenol (Kolbe reaction). The image likely shows cyclohexanol with –OH group on the ring suggesting it is phenol (cyclohexadienol i.e. phenol). Phenol + aq. NaOH gives sodium phenoxide; + CO2/H+ gives salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) via Kolbe reaction

questions.solution:
Answer (a) – Mechanism of dehydration of ethanol at 443 K with H+: In the first step, the H+ protonates the –OH group of ethanol to form an ethyl oxonium ion (CH3CH2–OH2+). In the second step, the C–O bond breaks heterolytically and water is expelled, generating the ethyl carbocation (CH3CH2+). In the third step, a proton is abstracted from the beta carbon (–CH3 group) by water acting as a base, and a pi bond forms, giving ethylene (CH2=CH2). The acid catalyst is regenerated.

Answer (b)(i): But-1-ene (CH3CH2CH=CH2) undergoes hydroboration-oxidation. This is an anti-Markovnikov addition of water. Boron adds to the less substituted carbon (C-1), and after oxidation with H2O2/OH–, the hydroxyl group appears at C-1. The major product is butan-1-ol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH).

Answer (b)(ii): The compound shown is phenol (hydroxybenzene). When phenol is treated with aqueous NaOH, it forms sodium phenoxide (C6H5ONa). When sodium phenoxide is treated with CO2 (Kolbe's reaction) followed by acidification with H+, electrophilic substitution of CO2 occurs ortho to the –OH group, yielding salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) as the major product.

पोटैशियम टेट्राहाइड्रॉक्सिडोज़िंकेट (II)

(ख) निम्नलिखित संकुलों को उनके विलयन की चालकता के बढ़ते हुए क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए :

questions.text_english:
(a) Write the formula for the following coordination compound :
Potassium tetrahydroxidozincate (II)

(b) Arrange the following complexes in the increasing order of conductivity of their solution :
[Cr(NH3)5Cl]Cl2, [Cr(NH3)3Cl3], [Cr(NH3)6]Cl3

(c) Identify the type of isomerism exhibited by the following complexes :
(i) [Co(NH3)5NO2]2+
(ii) [Co(en)3]Cl3

key_points: (a) K2[Zn(OH)4]
(b) [Cr(NH3)3Cl3] < [Cr(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 < [Cr(NH3)6]Cl3 (increasing number of ions in solution means increasing conductivity)
(c)(i) [Co(NH3)5NO2]2+ shows linkage isomerism (NO2 can coordinate through N as nitro or through O as nitrito)
(c)(ii) [Co(en)3]Cl3 shows optical isomerism (en is a bidentate ligand creating non-superimposable mirror images)

questions.solution:
Answer (a): Potassium tetrahydroxidozincate(II) contains potassium as the cation and [Zn(OH)4]2– as the complex anion. Zinc is in +2 oxidation state with four hydroxide ligands. The formula is K2[Zn(OH)4].

Answer (b): Conductivity depends on the number of ions produced per formula unit in solution. [Cr(NH3)3Cl3] gives 0 ions (non-electrolyte, all chlorides inside coordination sphere), so lowest conductivity. [Cr(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 gives 3 ions (1 complex cation + 2 Cl–). [Cr(NH3)6]Cl3 gives 4 ions (1 complex cation + 3 Cl–), so highest conductivity. Increasing order: [Cr(NH3)3Cl3] < [Cr(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 < [Cr(NH3)6]Cl3.

Answer (c)(i): [Co(NH3)5NO2]2+ exhibits linkage isomerism. The ambidentate ligand NO2– can bond to cobalt either through nitrogen (giving pentaamminenitrocobalt(III) ion) or through oxygen (giving pentaamminenitritocobalt(III) ion), giving two isomers.

Answer (c)(ii): [Co(en)3]Cl3 exhibits optical isomerism. The three bidentate ethylenediamine ligands create a chiral centre, giving two non-superimposable mirror images — d (dextrorotatory) and l (laevorotatory) forms.

questions.text_english:
(a) Which of the following is an allylic halide ?
(i) CH3–CH=CH–Br
(ii) CH2=CH–CH(Br)–CH3

(b) Out of chlorobenzene and 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene, which is more reactive towards nucleophilic substitution and why ?

(c) Which isomer of C4H9Cl has the lowest boiling point ?

key_points: (a) (ii) CH2=CH–CH(Br)–CH3 is the allylic halide because Br is on the carbon adjacent to the C=C double bond; (i) is a vinylic halide because Br is directly on the sp2 carbon of the double bond

(b) 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene is more reactive towards nucleophilic substitution because the three –NO2 groups (electron withdrawing) at ortho and para positions stabilize the Meisenheimer complex intermediate

(c) 2-chloro-2-methylpropane (tert-butyl chloride, (CH3)3CCl) has the lowest boiling point among C4H9Cl isomers due to its highly branched structure and smallest surface area for van der Waals interactions

questions.solution:
Answer (a): Option (ii) CH2=CH–CH(Br)–CH3 is the allylic halide, because the bromine atom is attached to the carbon that is adjacent (allylic position) to the carbon-carbon double bond. In option (i) CH3–CH=CH–Br, the bromine is directly attached to a doubly-bonded carbon (sp2), making it a vinylic halide, not an allylic halide.

Answer (b): 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene is far more reactive than chlorobenzene towards nucleophilic substitution. In nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr), the rate depends on the stability of the Meisenheimer complex (negatively charged intermediate). The three strongly electron-withdrawing –NO2 groups at the 2, 4, and 6 positions withdraw electron density from the ring and directly stabilize the negative charge in the Meisenheimer complex through resonance, making the reaction proceed readily. Chlorobenzene lacks such activating groups and is generally unreactive towards nucleophilic substitution.

Answer (c): Among the isomers of C4H9Cl (1-chlorobutane, 2-chlorobutane, 1-chloro-2-methylpropane, and 2-chloro-2-methylpropane), the most branched isomer — 2-chloro-2-methylpropane (tert-butyl chloride) — has the lowest boiling point (51°C). This is because greater branching reduces the surface area available for intermolecular van der Waals (London dispersion) forces, resulting in weaker intermolecular attraction and a lower boiling point.

The following initial rate data were obtained for the reaction :
2NO (g) + Br2 (g) → 2NOBr (g)
Expt. No. | [NO]/mol L–1 | [Br2]/mol L–1 | Initial Rate (mol L–1 s–1)
1 | 0·05 | 0·05 | 1·0 × 10–3

3 | 0·15 | 0·05 | 9·0 × 10–3

(b) Calculate the rate constant (k).
(c) Determine the rate of reaction when concentration of NO and Br2 are 0·4 M and 0·2 M, respectively.

key_points: (a) Order w.r.t. NO = 2 (from experiments 1 and 3: [NO] triples, rate increases 9-fold = 3²); Order w.r.t. Br2 = 1 (from experiments 1 and 2: [Br2] triples, rate triples)

questions.solution:
Answer (a): Comparing experiments 1 and 2, [NO] is constant and [Br2] increases 3-fold (0.05 to 0.15); rate increases 3-fold (1.0×10–3 to 3.0×10–3). Therefore order w.r.t. Br2 = 1. Comparing experiments 1 and 3, [Br2] is constant and [NO] increases 3-fold (0.05 to 0.15); rate increases 9-fold (1.0×10–3 to 9.0×10–3 = 3²). Therefore order w.r.t. NO = 2. The rate law is: Rate = k[NO]²[Br2], and overall order = 3.

Answer (b): Using data from experiment 1: 1.0×10–3 = k × (0.05)² × (0.05) = k × 2.5×10–3 × 5×10–2 = k × 1.25×10–4. Therefore k = 1.0×10–3 / 1.25×10–4 = 8 mol–2 L2 s–1.

Answer (c): Rate = k[NO]²[Br2] = 8 × (0.4)² × (0.2) = 8 × 0.16 × 0.2 = 8 × 0.032 = 0.256 mol L–1 s–1.

जब किसी चालकता सेल को 0·05 M KCl विलयन से भरा जाता है, तो 25°C पर इसका प्रतिरोध 100 ओम है । जब उसी सेल को 0·02 M AgNO3 विलयन से भरा गया, तो प्रतिरोध 90 ओम था । AgNO3 विलयन की चालकता और मोलर चालकता परिकलित कीजिए ।
(दिया गया है : 0·05 M KCl विलयन की चालकता = 1·35 × 10–2 ohm–1 cm–1)
questions.text_english:
When a certain conductivity cell was filled with 0·05 M KCl solution, it has a resistance of 100 ohm at 25°C. When the same cell was filled with 0·02 M AgNO3 solution, the resistance was 90 ohm. Calculate the conductivity and molar conductivity of AgNO3 solution.
(Given : Conductivity of 0·05 M KCl solution = 1·35 × 10–2 ohm–1 cm–1)

key_points: Cell constant = conductivity of KCl × resistance of KCl = 1.35×10–2 × 100 = 1.35 cm–1
Conductivity of AgNO3 = cell constant / resistance = 1.35 / 90 = 1.5 × 10–2 ohm–1 cm–1
Molar conductivity = (conductivity × 1000) / molarity = (1.5×10–2 × 1000) / 0.02 = 750 ohm–1 cm2 mol–1

questions.solution:
Step 1 – Find the cell constant: Cell constant (G*) = conductivity of KCl × resistance of KCl = 1.35×10–2 ohm–1 cm–1 × 100 ohm = 1.35 cm–1.

Step 2 – Find conductivity of AgNO3: Conductivity (κ) = Cell constant / Resistance = 1.35 cm–1 / 90 ohm = 1.5 × 10–2 ohm–1 cm–1.

Step 3 – Find molar conductivity: Molar conductivity (Λm) = (κ × 1000) / M = (1.5×10–2 × 1000) / 0.02 = 15 / 0.02 = 750 ohm–1 cm2 mol–1.

Therefore, the conductivity of AgNO3 solution is 1.5 × 10–2 ohm–1 cm–1 and its molar conductivity is 750 ohm–1 cm2 mol–1.

questions.text: संयोजकता आबंध सिद्धांत (VBT) उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों के बनने, चुंबकीय व्यवहार और ज्यामितीय आकृतियों का यथोचित स्पष्टीकरण देता है जबकि 'क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत' उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों में विद्यमान केन्द्रीय धातु परमाणु/आयन के d-कक्षकों की ऊर्जा की समानता पर विभिन्न क्रिस्टल क्षेत्रों के प्रभाव (लिगन्डों को बिंदु आवेश मानते हुए उनके द्वारा प्रदत्त प्रभाव) पर आधारित है । प्रबल तथा दुर्बल क्रिस्टल क्षेत्रों में d-कक्षकों के विपाटन (splitting) से विभिन्न इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास प्राप्त होते हैं । क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत यह मानता है कि उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों का रंग इलेक्ट्रॉन के d-d संक्रमण (transition) के कारण होता है । उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों की धातुकर्म प्रक्रमों, विश्लेषणात्मक तथा औषध रसायन के क्षेत्र में महत्त्वपूर्ण अनुप्रयोग हैं ।
questions.text_english: The Valence Bond Theory (VBT) explains the formation, magnetic behaviour and geometrical shapes of coordination compounds whereas 'The Crystal Field Theory' for coordination compounds is based on the effect of different crystal fields (provided by ligands taken as point charges), on the degeneracy of d-orbital energies of the central metal atom/ion. The splitting of the d-orbitals provides different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields. The crystal field theory attributes the colour of the coordination compounds to d-d transition of the electron. Coordination compounds find extensive applications in metallurgical processes, analytical and medicinal chemistry.

sub_questions.text: क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र विपाटन ऊर्जा क्या है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What is crystal field splitting energy ?

key_points: The energy difference between the two sets of d-orbitals (eg and t2g) after splitting in a crystal field is called crystal field splitting energy (Δ or 10Dq)

sub_questions.solution: Crystal field splitting energy (denoted as Δo for octahedral or Δt for tetrahedral) is the energy difference between the higher energy set of d-orbitals (eg: dx2–y2 and dz2) and the lower energy set (t2g: dxy, dyz, dxz) after they are split by the electrostatic field of the surrounding ligands. It determines the colour and magnetic properties of coordination compounds.

sub_questions.text: क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत के आधार पर संकुल [Ti(H2O)6]3+ के बैंगनी रंग का कारण दीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Give reason for the violet colour of the complex [Ti(H2O)6]3+ on the basis of crystal field theory.

key_points: Ti3+ has one d-electron in t2g; it absorbs yellow-green visible light and undergoes d-d transition from t2g to eg; the complementary colour violet is transmitted

sub_questions.solution: In [Ti(H2O)6]3+, titanium is in the +3 oxidation state with one d-electron (d1 configuration). This single electron occupies the lower energy t2g orbital. When white light falls on the complex, the d-electron absorbs a photon of yellow-green light (around 500 nm) and gets excited to the higher energy eg orbital (d-d transition). The complementary colour of yellow-green is violet, which is transmitted and perceived by the eye. This explains the violet colour of the complex.

sub_questions.text: [Cr(NH3)6]3+ अनुचुम्बकीय है जबकि [Ni(CN)4]2– प्रतिचुम्बकीय है । व्याख्या कीजिए, क्यों । [परमाणु क्रमांक : Cr = 24, Ni = 28]
sub_questions.text_english: [Cr(NH3)6]3+ is paramagnetic while [Ni(CN)4]2– is diamagnetic. Explain why. [Atomic No. : Cr = 24, Ni = 28]

key_points: Cr (Z=24): [Ar]3d54s1; Cr3+ is 3d3. In [Cr(NH3)6]3+, NH3 is a strong field ligand but with 3d3 configuration, t2g³ arrangement has 3 unpaired electrons — paramagnetic
Ni (Z=28): [Ar]3d84s2; Ni2+ is 3d8. CN– is a very strong field ligand causing pairing; in square planar [Ni(CN)4]2–, all electrons are paired — diamagnetic

sub_questions.solution:
Chromium (Cr, Z=24) has the electronic configuration [Ar]3d54s1. Cr3+ has the configuration 3d3. In [Cr(NH3)6]3+, although NH3 is a strong field ligand, the 3 d-electrons occupy three separate t2g orbitals (t2g3), all unpaired (by Hund's rule). The presence of 3 unpaired electrons makes the complex paramagnetic.

Nickel (Ni, Z=28) has the configuration [Ar]3d84s2. Ni2+ has the configuration 3d8. CN– is a very strong field ligand that causes large crystal field splitting and forces pairing of electrons. In [Ni(CN)4]2–, the complex adopts a square planar geometry and the 8 d-electrons pair up completely, leaving no unpaired electrons. Therefore, [Ni(CN)4]2– is diamagnetic.

questions.text_english: Batteries and fuel cells are very useful forms of galvanic cell. Any battery or cell that we use as a source of electrical energy is basically a galvanic cell. However, for a battery to be of practical use it should be reasonably light, compact and its voltage should not vary appreciably during its use. There are mainly two types of batteries — primary batteries and secondary batteries. In the primary batteries, the reaction occurs only once and after use over a period of time the battery becomes dead and cannot be reused again, whereas the secondary batteries are rechargeable. Production of electricity by thermal plants is not a very efficient method and is a major source of pollution. To solve this problem, galvanic cells are designed in such a way that energy of combustion of fuels is directly converted into electrical energy, and these are known as fuel cells. One such fuel cell was used in the Apollo space programme.

sub_questions.text: प्राथमिक बैटरियाँ, संचायक बैटरियों से किस प्रकार भिन्न होती हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: How do primary batteries differ from secondary batteries ?

key_points: Primary batteries are non-rechargeable (reaction occurs only once); secondary batteries are rechargeable (can be recharged by passing electric current)

sub_questions.solution: In primary batteries, the cell reaction occurs only once and the battery cannot be recharged after it is discharged. Examples include dry cells and mercury cells. In secondary batteries (also called accumulators), the cell reaction is reversible and the battery can be recharged by passing electric current through it in the reverse direction. Examples include lead storage batteries and nickel-cadmium cells.

sub_questions.text: मक्यूरी सेल का सेल विभव 1·35 V होता है तथा सम्पूर्ण कार्य-अवधि में स्थिर रहता है । कारण दीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: The cell potential of Mercury cell is 1·35 V, and remains constant during its life. Give reason.

key_points: In mercury cell, the overall reaction does not involve any ions in solution; the electrolyte is paste of KOH and ZnO and concentrations do not change during discharge, so cell potential remains constant

sub_questions.solution: In the mercury cell, the anode is zinc amalgam (Zn-Hg) and the cathode is mercury(II) oxide (HgO) in a paste of KOH and ZnO. The overall cell reaction is: Zn(Hg) + HgO → ZnO + Hg. Since none of the reactants or products are ions in solution — the electrolyte does not change its concentration during the discharge — the cell potential remains constant at 1.35 V throughout its life, unlike ordinary dry cells where solution concentrations change.

sub_questions.text: लेड संचायक बैटरी के पुन:आवेशन (रिचार्जिंग) में सम्मिलित अभिक्रियाएँ लिखिए ।

key_points: Anode (during recharging): PbSO4 + 2H2O → PbO2 + SO42– + 4H+ + 2e–
Cathode (during recharging): PbSO4 + 2e– → Pb + SO42–
Overall: 2PbSO4 + 2H2O → Pb + PbO2 + 2H2SO4

sub_questions.solution: During recharging of the lead storage battery, the cell is connected to an external source of electricity and the discharge reactions are reversed. At the anode (positive plate, PbSO4 is oxidized): PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l) → PbO2(s) + SO42–(aq) + 4H+(aq) + 2e–. At the cathode (negative plate, PbSO4 is reduced): PbSO4(s) + 2e– → Pb(s) + SO42–(aq). The overall recharging reaction is: 2PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l) → Pb(s) + PbO2(s) + 2H2SO4(aq). The sulphuric acid concentration is restored and the electrodes are regenerated.

questions.solution:
Answer (a)(i)(1): Zinc, Cadmium, and Mercury have completely filled d-orbitals (d10 configuration). Since all d-orbitals are fully occupied, there are no unpaired d-electrons available for strong metallic bonding. The metallic bonding in these elements is consequently weak, which results in lower melting and boiling points compared to other transition metals.

Answer (a)(i)(2): Both Cr2+ and Mn3+ are d4 species. Cr2+ (3d4) can easily lose one electron to achieve the stable half-filled d3 configuration, making it a strong reducing agent. Mn3+ (3d4) can easily gain one electron to achieve the stable half-filled d5 configuration, making it a strong oxidizing agent. The tendency to achieve the stable half-filled d3 or d5 sub-shell drives these opposite behaviors.

Answer (a)(i)(3): Although copper lies after nickel in the activity series (suggesting it should not readily form ions), the high hydration enthalpy of Cu2+ ion provides sufficient energy to overcome the energy required for ionization. Moreover, copper has an exceptional electronic configuration ([Ar]3d104s1), and the second ionization energy (removing from 3d10 to give 3d9) is lower than expected, making Cu2+ formation more favorable. Thus E° for Cu2+/Cu is positive (+0.34 V).

Answer (a)(ii)(1): On strong heating: 2KMnO4 → K2MnO4 + MnO2 + O2. Manganese is reduced from +7 to +6 and +4.

Answer (a)(ii)(2): Cr2O72– + 6I– + 14H+ → 2Cr3+ + 3I2 + 7H2O. Chromium is reduced from +6 to +3 and iodide is oxidized to iodine.

(a) (i) At the same temperature, CO2 gas is more soluble in water than O2 gas. Which one of them will have higher value of KH and why ?
(ii) How does the size of blood cells change when placed in an aqueous solution containing more than 0·9% (mass/volume) sodium chloride ?
(iii) 1 molal aqueous solution of an electrolyte A2B3 is 60% ionized. Calculate the boiling point of the solution.
(Given : Kb for H2O = 0·52 K kg mol–1)

OR

(b) (i) The vapour pressures of A and B at 25°C are 75 mm Hg and 25 mm Hg, respectively. If A and B are mixed such that the mole fraction of A in the mixture is 0·4, then calculate the mole fraction of B in vapour phase.
(ii) Define colligative property. Which colligative property is preferred for the molar mass determination of macromolecules ?
(iii) Why are equimolar solutions of sodium chloride and glucose not isotonic ?

key_points: (a)(i) O2 will have higher KH; Henry's law: KH is higher for less soluble gases; CO2 is more soluble so has lower KH
(a)(ii) The blood cells shrink (undergo crenation/plasmolysis) because the external solution is hypertonic; water moves out of cells by osmosis
(b)(i) Mole fraction of B in liquid = 0.6; PA = 75×0.4 = 30 mm Hg; PB = 25×0.6 = 15 mm Hg; Ptotal = 45 mm Hg; mole fraction of B in vapour = 15/45 = 1/3 ≈ 0.333
(b)(ii) Colligative property depends only on number of solute particles, not their nature; osmotic pressure is preferred for macromolecules as it gives measurable values at very low concentrations
(b)(iii) NaCl dissociates into 2 ions (Na+ and Cl–) while glucose does not dissociate; equal molar solutions have different particle concentrations, hence different osmotic pressures

questions.solution:
Answer (a)(i): According to Henry's law, the solubility of a gas is inversely proportional to its Henry's law constant (KH). Since CO2 is more soluble in water than O2, CO2 has a lower KH. Therefore, O2 has the higher value of KH.

Answer (a)(ii): A solution containing more than 0.9% NaCl is hypertonic (higher osmotic pressure than blood). When blood cells are placed in this solution, water flows out of the cells by osmosis (from lower solute concentration inside to higher outside). As a result, the blood cells shrink in size — a process called crenation.

Answer (a)(iii): A2B3 dissociates as A2B3 → 2A3+ + 3B2–, giving 5 ions per formula unit (n=5). With 60% ionization (α=0.6): Van't Hoff factor i = 1 + (n–1)α = 1 + (5–1)×0.6 = 1 + 2.4 = 3.4. Elevation in boiling point: ΔTb = i × Kb × m = 3.4 × 0.52 × 1 = 1.768 K. Boiling point of solution = 100 + 1.768 = 101.768°C ≈ 101.77°C.

questions.text_english:
Answer any five questions of the following :
(a) N,N-diethyl-benzenesulphonamide is insoluble in alkali. Give reason.
(b) Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction. Why ?
(c) Write a simple chemical test to distinguish between methylamine and aniline.
(d) Write the chemical reaction involved in Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.
(e) How will you convert aniline to p-bromoaniline ?
(f) Complete the following reaction :
[Benzenediazonium chloride] + (i) HBF4 / (ii) NaNO2/Cu, Δ →
(g) Write the structures of A and B in the following reaction :
Benzoic acid → (NH3/Δ) → A → (Br2 + NaOH) → B

key_points: (a) N,N-diethylbenzenesulphonamide has no N–H bond; sulphonamides with N–H are acidic and dissolve in alkali by losing that proton; without N–H it cannot form a soluble sodium salt

(b) Aniline acts as a Lewis base and forms a salt with the Lewis acid catalyst AlCl3 used in Friedel-Crafts; the ammonium salt (C6H5NH3+ AlCl4–) formed is insoluble and deactivates the ring, preventing reaction

(c) Carbylamine test: both react with CHCl3/KOH; methylamine gives methylisocyanide (foul smell); OR: bromine water test: aniline gives white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline while methylamine does not give precipitate; OR: diazonium salt test
(d) Gabriel synthesis: phthalimide reacts with KOH → potassium phthalimide; then reacts with alkyl halide (RX) → N-alkylphthalimide; then hydrolysis with HCl/H2O or N2H4 gives primary amine (RNH2)
(e) Protect –NH2 by acetylation (CH3COCl or (CH3CO)2O) → acetanilide; then brominate with Br2/CH3COOH to get p-bromoacetanilide; then hydrolyze with NaOH/H2O to get p-bromoaniline
(f) C6H5N2+Cl– + HBF4 → C6H5N2+BF4– (diazonium tetrafluoroborate); then NaNO2/Cu, Δ → C6H5NO2 (nitrobenzene) via Sandmeyer-type reaction / or fluorobenzene via Balz-Schiemann
(g) Benzoic acid + NH3/Δ → A = benzamide (C6H5CONH2); Benzamide + Br2 + NaOH (Hoffmann bromamide) → B = aniline (C6H5NH2)

questions.solution:
Answer (a): N,N-diethylbenzenesulphonamide has nitrogen atoms substituted with two ethyl groups, leaving no N–H bond. Sulphonamides are soluble in alkali only when they have an acidic N–H hydrogen, which can be removed by a base to form a soluble sodium salt. Since there is no N–H in N,N-diethylbenzenesulphonamide, it cannot react with alkali and remains insoluble.

Answer (b): Aniline (C6H5NH2) acts as a Lewis base. When it encounters the Lewis acid catalyst AlCl3 required for Friedel-Crafts reaction, it immediately forms an insoluble coordination complex (salt: C6H5NH3+AlCl4–). This salt deactivates the amino group by converting it to –NH3+ (an electron-withdrawing group) and also removes AlCl3 from the reaction mixture, making Friedel-Crafts alkylation or acylation impossible.

Answer (c): Bromine water test: when aniline is added to bromine water, an immediate white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline is formed. Methylamine, being an aliphatic amine, does not give a precipitate with bromine water under normal conditions. Thus, aniline can be distinguished from methylamine by the white precipitate formed with Br2 water.

Answer (d): Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves three steps: (1) Phthalimide reacts with alcoholic KOH to form potassium phthalimide (K+ ion replaces the N–H hydrogen). (2) Potassium phthalimide reacts with an alkyl halide (RX) to give N-substituted phthalimide (N-alkylphthalimide). (3) The N-alkylphthalimide undergoes acidic or hydrazine hydrolysis to give the corresponding primary amine (RNH2) along with phthalic acid or phthalhydrazide.

Answer (e): To convert aniline to p-bromoaniline: Step 1 — Acetylate aniline by reacting with acetic anhydride or acetyl chloride to get acetanilide (C6H5NHCOCH3). This protects the amino group, reducing its activating effect. Step 2 — Brominate acetanilide with Br2 in acetic acid; the –NHCOCH3 group is less activating, giving predominantly the para isomer, p-bromoacetanilide. Step 3 — Hydrolyze p-bromoacetanilide with NaOH/H2O (or HCl) to remove the acetyl protecting group, yielding p-bromoaniline (4-bromoaniline).
